newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada rejects U.S. plea for grain export limits.
newsitem.headline: Canada rejects U.S. plea for grain export limits.

text.p: Canada rejected another U.S. plea to limit its grain exports, Canadian government officials said on Friday after a meeting with senior U.S. officials.
"They did express concerns about the levels of exports of Canadian wheat," Foreign Affairs spokesman Malcolm McKechnie said in a telephone interview.
"We in kind responded that we have no intention to limit our exports."

Farmers in the northern U.S. plains have complained for years of an unfair level of Canadian wheat exports. The Clinton administration has told Canada it would take action if the shipments exceeded 1.5 million tonnes a year, a level Canada is close to reaching now.
But Canada has maintained that it was within its rights to export as much grain as it wanted to the United States.
The United States may be looking at ways to increase its own grain exports into Canada rather than push for a cap on Canadian grain exports, officials said.
The senior officials' meeting was the second such meeting on Canadian grain exports in the past three months, and officials would continue to discuss the matter, McKechnie said.
"Progress was made but further work is required," he said.
In 1995, Canada agreed to cap exports at 1.5 million tonnes a year, but that agreement has expired.
